transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Head of Data Platforms, CedarPoint), Omar Ruiz (Procurement), Dina Shah (Security), Samir Patel (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya my solutions engineer is here. Quick agenda — run through procurement gating, security questions, what a pilot looks like and timings. Laura — you wanna kick us off with priorities?

[00:27] Laura: Yeah thanks Evan. We're trying to — um — standardize LLM inference across some product teams. Primary asks from finance/procurement are clear: DPA/MSA terms, pricing ranges, and SLAs. From security, Dina's team needs clarity on KMS and egress. Timeline is a bit tight, procurement wants a decision window within three weeks if numbers look ok.

[00:48] Omar: Right, procurement's main blocker is committed capacity vs on-demand billing. Finance wants a committed monthly baseline otherwise it goes back to the pricing committee. Also we have to show vendor SOC2 and DPA samples before we move into legal review.

[01:15] Dina: For security — we need key management, audit logs for model requests, and an option for private deployment (VPC or on-prem) because of regulated PII in some payloads. Also data residency: EU West preference, ideally Frankfurt.

[01:40] Priya: Thanks, that helps. Quick clarification: when you say private deployment — do you mean a fully private plane with customer-controlled VPC peering, or is it ok to have dedicated but hosted capacity with customer-keyed KMS? There's a tradeoff on time-to-prod.

[02:02] Laura: Ideally customer-keyed KMS is fine as long as logs and keys are customer-owned. On-prem would be a later-phase. For pilot we want to test in Frankfurt with committed throughput so teams can estimate latency and spend.

[02:30] Evan: Makes sense. High level from Redwood: we offer Hosted API for fastest path, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads. For procurement, committed dedicated capacity maps well to a monthly commit that finance likes.

[03:00] Priya: On performance: we can run a canary benchmark that mimics your production profile — e.g., 1k concurrent users with an average 2k token/session, mixed short and long contexts. We'll measure p50/p95 latency, cold start, and token throughput.

[03:25] Samir: Quick Q — how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? We have a lot of repeated prompts.

[03:40] Priya: We do automatic prefix/K V cache — sorry the transcript system wrote K V cash earlier — but yes, KV cache and smart batching to reduce token cost and latency. We can show how batching and caching reduce the per-token cost on sample traces.

[04:05] Omar: On the legal side: can you share a sample MSA with the typical liability caps and DPA? Our counsel will want to see indemnities and subprocessors.

[04:18] Evan: Yep, we'll send a standard MSA + DPA redline for reference. Note: many enterprise customers ask for a SOC2 report and ISO attestation. We can provide SOC2 Type II link.

[04:35] Dina: Also, does Redwood support customer-managed KMS? And HSM-backed key storage? That's a hard requirement for some datasets.

[04:48] Priya: Yes — we integrate with customer KMS providers and offer HSM options in Private deployments. For Hosted, you can bring your own key via our KMS integrations; there's a short tech preflight to enable envelope encryption.

[05:05] Laura: Ok, on pricing — can you give committed tiers and example invoices so finance can model CAPEX vs OPEX?

[05:18] Evan: We'll send a pricing sheet with committed monthly and burst allowances. Two options: 1) Dedicated reserved with monthly commit (lower per-token unit cost), 2) Hosted on-demand with higher unit costs but no commit. We'll include an example showing egress fees and quantization savings.

[05:40] Omar: GOV question — are there egress fees from EU to US, for logging/analytics? We need to know if cross-region egress adds material cost.

[05:55] Priya: Egress is charged per egressed GB based on region. If you keep everything in EU-West region and host observability there, you can avoid cross-region egress. We'll call out estimated egress using your expected token volumes.

[06:15] Samir: On network: what does the VPC peering look like? Any firewall ports, proxies?

[06:28] Evan: Typical VPC peering with minimal ports — TLS over 443. We'll share the VPC peering checklist and a preflight doc. Also support for private link in certain clouds.

[06:45] Dina: Audit logs — we need request-level logs and retention control. Are logs exportable to our SIEM?

[06:55] Priya: Yes, audit logs are exportable to customer SIEM via secure delivery; retention is configurable depending on plan. For Private deployments you can keep logs entirely inside your network.

[07:10] Laura: Great. One concern — latency SLOs. Our product teams expect p95 under 500ms for short prompts. Is that realistic?

[07:25] Priya: For short prompts and optimized models, p95 under 500ms is achievable on Dedicated in Frankfurt for typical loads. For long-context 8k tokens it will be higher. We'll provide benchmark numbers. Cold starts add a bit as well.

[07:48] Omar: Procurement will ask: what is SLA downtime credit? And what's the remedy when SLA breached?

[07:58] Evan: Standard SLA with uptime targets and credits tied to monthly uptime percentage; we'll include the SLA language in the MSA draft. For critical enterprise, higher SLAs can be negotiated in Dedicated contracts.

[08:15] Laura: Ok, timeline recap — we want the MSA/DPA and pricing to review by legal/finance this week if possible so procurement can do their gating next week.

[08:28] Evan: We'll prioritize sending docs today/tomorrow. Priya will run the Frankfurt benchmark and share numbers by next Tuesday.

[08:40] (Later — technical deep dive section)

[25:00] Priya: Running the bench — we usually test throughput vs latency curves. For example, at 250 qps with 1k token avg we'll show p50/p95, and then scale to 1k qps. We can also simulate cache-hit rates.

[30:12] Samir: If we go with dedicated reserved capacity, how long is the ramp? Can we spin up more GPUs quickly?

[30:25] Priya: Dedicated pools can autoscale within configured policies, but a committed pool gives you predictable baseline. Burst capacity is available but may take a few minutes to provision depending on region.

[32:10] Dina: Legal — subprocessors. We need list of third parties that will process data (cloud providers, logging vendors).

[32:25] Evan: We'll include a subprocessor list in the DPA and keep it updated during onboarding.

[35:40] Omar: For the procurement path — if we sign a short pilot commit (30 days) with a small monthly baseline, does Redwood allow rolling to full committed in 60 days?

[35:55] Evan: Yes we support staged rollouts — pilot => committed => enterprise. We'll include a sample rollover clause in the MSA.

[40:05] Laura: Any blockers you see from our side?

[40:15] Priya: From the tech side, network peering and keys are the main setup. From legal, expedite DPA review. From procurement, we need the pricing scenarios and examples.

[41:00] Dina: One micro point — we need to know if logs can be hashed/anonymized before leaving prod — some payloads include PII.

[41:12] Priya: Yes we can configure redaction/anonymization in the pipeline and show recommended patterns. We'll include a doc on data minimization best practices.

[45:30] Evan: Quick recap — action items assigned, we'll send MSA/DPA redlines + SOC2 by 2026-08-12, Priya runs benchmarks and shares by 2026-08-17, schedule network preflight the week of 2026-08-24. Omar will confirm procurement decision owner and timeline.

[45:55] Omar: Sounds good. One ask — can you put the pilot pricing in a single slide so finance can quickly sign off?

[46:06] Evan: Yes, we'll prepare a single-page cost summary with committed vs on-demand and egress sensitivity.

[46:25] Laura: Thanks — that's it from us.

[46:30] Evan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with doc links.

End notes: References shared during call: pricing deck (link), SOC2 report (link), VPC peering checklist (link), benchmark template spreadsheet (link).

Transcript quirks: occasional mislabels and filler (uh, mm), some product names transcribed oddly (e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedicat-ed), KV cache transcribed as K V cash in a couple places.
